cells: CONCLUSION & REFLECTION  |  Evaluate THROUGHOUT; draw things TOGETHER at the end
The conclusion isn't a summary of everything done. In a few focused thoughts, answer the aim with the key evidence, connect to the intended beneficiary, and look forward.
Keep justification/limitations at the relevant data or mathematical work, and reflect when something changes the interpretation. Don't save all evaluation for the end.
Use earlier student-authored result records, interpretation and key limitations as references—not material to copy into a second section or graphs to repeat.
Future directions should be prompted by what the student FOUND: What could be investigated NEXT, why would it matter, and what mathematics/evidence would help?
Keep the default prompt sequence compact. Contextual examples and an anti-repetition checklist are available ON REQUEST. No guaranteed marks, automated conclusion or rigid structure.

While performing/interpreting a mathematical method
Why this maths? What do the results mean, and how do the actual assumptions/uncertainty affect them?

C50 · ongoing exploration
As further results change the question or original plan

Record reasoning as it develops, not as a retrospective 'what went wrong' chapter.
Student's revisions, alternative checks, next steps
Don't paste an entire project diary into the ending.
Reference the change only if it matters to the overall answer.
Agreed
C34U · unexpected result
When actual output differs from prediction, not only at the end
What differs? Is there a useful alternative view, check or restricted conclusion?
A justified detour is good mathematical reflection, even if no favourable pattern emerges.
Original prediction, real observation, considered vs tested explanation
Don't claim an untested explanation was proved.
Only mention important unresolved questions and their future implications.
Agreed
C60–C64 · conclusion
When enough mathematics exists to provide an answer or explain why not
What is the overall answer, what does it mean, and what sensible investigation might follow?
Synthesize evidence already explained; leave methodological detail where it first occurred.
Aim, beneficiary, 1–3 key result references and evidence scope
No replay of calculations, charts, sampling, assumptions or every limitation.
A concise ending and future question, in the student's voice.
Agreed
C70/C90 · editorial check
When reviewing the completed written IA
Have I made reflection visible throughout without duplicating it in my conclusion?
Check coherence and correct placement, not that enough reflection paragraphs exist.
Result-by-result reflections, existing conclusion draft
No final evaluation dump or forced heading order.
Offer links to relevant earlier sections for targeted improvements.

POSSIBLE NEXT STEPS  |  Match to the student's REAL findings; at most two suggestions, only on request
ID
Investigation/outcome
Required actual previous finding
Optional student-facing next-step nudge
Possible further mathematics/evidence
Why it would add value
Avoid
Stage
Status
Statistics · association observed
Actual correlation/association interpreted, causal claim limited
Could a justified third variable or different context help explain the association?
Suggest a specific relevant confounder/stratification or independent comparison and why it matters.
May clarify generalisability or mechanism, not guarantee causation.
Avoid automatically saying 'prove cause and effect' or forcing PMCC again.
Agreed
Statistics · weak or inconclusive relationship
Student actually found little clear association
Would a better-targeted variable or different question make the inference more informative?
Offer a more focused investigation aim or one mathematically justified comparison. No need for a formal research-question template.
Could show whether no association is meaningful or a limitation of study design.
Avoid fishing for a significant result or pretending it must exist.
Agreed
Statistics · sampling limits restrict the answer
Actual representativeness/coverage concern was confirmed
Would a broader or more carefully selected group change the population the conclusions apply to?
Name the missing/biased group or a better frame, and what estimate would be compared.
May increase the defensible scope of advice.
Not simply 'collect more data'; justify the mathematical benefit.
Agreed
Statistics · groups differ or are unexpectedly similar
Student made a genuine group comparison
Would comparing an additional meaningful group or controlling for a relevant variable help explain the difference?
Specify new group/context or variable and intended comparison.
Tests whether pattern generalises or differs by a known condition.
Don't invent group differences or demand an extra hypothesis test.
Agreed
Statistics · distribution looks unusual
Student actually found skew/clusters or non-normal shape
Would contrasting another legitimate subgroup/period help understand the distribution?
Name a meaningful comparison and why it could affect the apparent shape.
Can explore a contextual explanation for grouping/skewness.
No forced normal distribution or random additional charts.
Agreed
Modelling · fitted relationship seems useful
Model has actually been fitted/tested and range noted
What additional conditions or independent measurements would assess its predictive usefulness?
Suggest a new realistic test range or held-out observation where feasible.
Shows whether model survives beyond calibration context.
Don't automatically claim the model is valid everywhere.
Agreed
Modelling · model accuracy/fit proved limited
Real model discrepancy or assumption issue was confirmed
Would changing one relevant assumption, parameter or model form address the observed discrepancy?
Specify the particular assumption/range/model candidate and the mathematical test.
Could explain residual structure or improve reliable predictions.
Avoid vague 'use better maths' or claiming a model was wrong without testing.
Agreed
Optimisation · practical choice depends on constraints
An actual feasible optimum or trade-off was found
What extra constraint or different objective would change the optimal decision?
Choose a real constraint such as budget/geometry/material or a genuine second objective.
Could reveal a trade-off important to the intended beneficiary.
Only relevant if optimisation was actually done; not just planned in IA proposal.
Agreed
Measurement-driven model · key uncertainty mattered
Recorded source/measurement uncertainty affects result
Could higher-quality evidence meaningfully distinguish between two plausible outcomes?
Identify which variable's accuracy and what decision it would alter.
A justified improvement in precision may make results more useful.
Do not frame 'difficulty with equipment' as the limitation or claim arbitrarily smaller error.
Agreed
Theoretical · conjecture/proof has scope
Investigation has a demonstrated pattern/counterexample or restricted theorem
Could the result generalise to another case, dimension or different mathematical condition?
Name exact changed condition and potential proof/counterexample question.
Extends mathematical understanding beyond the current proven case.
Do not present several tested examples as a proof.
Agreed
Unexpected finding still not explained
A genuine unresolved discrepancy is recorded
Which one alternative view or mathematical check could distinguish your leading explanations?
A targeted counterexample, different valid model or sensitivity comparison.
Shows a mathematically motivated continuation of honest uncertainty.
Do not retcon the original prediction or invent a tested explanation.
Agreed
No meaningful extension identified
Student has a coherent supported answer; no further question is obvious
Would ending with the justified answer be stronger than inventing an extension?
Allow None/not sure yet; possibly mention a genuine boundary without a new experiment.
An honest conclusion is preferable to filler.
Future steps encouraged, not compulsory invented research.
Agreed
